records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:6 — The new client-side pagination flow has no tests for an exact-full page or empty group, so its page-boundary behavior is unverified.
records.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial client-side pagination logic (currentPage, totalPages, next/previous actions in admin-group.js.es6, plus model.findMembers offset/limit handling), and no tests in this PR cover it — the spec changes only exercise the Rails controllers. The concern is specific, grounded in added code, and non-bug in nature; notably the totalPages formula Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 would report an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, making the flagged boundary cases genuinely risky.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Adding members performs an individual user lookup for every unbounded comma-separated username, creating linear database work for a single request.
records.rationale: The new add_members action in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb does `usernames.split(",").each { ... User.find_by_username(username) ... }`, which issues one query per username in an unbounded, client-controlled comma-separated list — a real, specific scalability/DoS-ish concern introduced by this diff, but not a correctness defect. It is accurately grounded in the diff and a maintainer would plausibly want to bound the input or batch the lookup (e.g., User.where(username: list)).

records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — The new paginated members response and its changed JSON shape have no request coverage for pagination bounds or metadata, leaving the public membership contract unverified.
records.rationale: The diff rewrites groups_controller.rb#members into a new paginated contract (render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }) with changed defaults (limit 50, unbounded user-supplied limit/offset applied to non-automatic groups too). The spec changes in this diff cover only Admin::GroupsController; no request spec exercises the new public endpoint, its pagination bounds, or the meta shape — so the newly introduced public JSON contract is unverified. This is a specific, non-bug test-coverage gap grounded in the diff.
records.stripped_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19 — The new paginated members response and its changed JSON shape have no request coverage for pagination bounds or metadata, leaving the public membership contract unverified.

records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint accepts an uncapped limit, allowing one request to load and serialize an entire large group.
records.rationale: The diff changes the public members endpoint from a hardcoded cap (200 for automatic groups) to `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound, so a client can request the entire membership of a large group in one query/serialization pass. This is a real, specific, diff-grounded concern (a plausible DoS/data-exposure surface), but it describes a resource-limitation weakness rather than clearly incorrect behavior, so it qualifies as an important non-bug advisory.
records.stripped_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint accepts an uncapped limit, allowing one request to load and serialize an entire large group.
